# Weekly Market Briefing — July 12, 2026

## 1. Market Regime: Cautiously Risk-On, "Higher-for-Longer" Backdrop
The macro tape reads constructive but rate-wary. The **10Y sits at 4.57%** (▲0.03 MoM), the **3M bill at 3.69%**, leaving a normal, upward-sloping **+0.88 curve** — no recession signal. **VIX at 15.03** (▼7.19 MoM) confirms a benign volatility regime, while a firming **DXY of 100.97** (▲1.22) reflects the Fed's hawkish tilt. Broad-market factor readings lean risk-on: momentum dominates value across the board (SPY Momentum **71** vs Value **61**; QQQ Momentum **89**; IWM **84**). At the mid-June FOMC — the first with Kevin Warsh as chair — the Fed struck a hawkish tone, bumping its 2026 inflation forecast to 3.6% from 2.7% and nudging its dot plot to 3.8%, signaling rates will stay higher for longer.

## 2. This Week's News
- **CPI looms (Tue July 14).** Expect a seemingly contradictory print — the headline monthly number will likely look surprisingly soft or even negative, but a one-month dip in energy prices doesn't mean the macro picture has changed.
- **Earnings season kicks off.** Q2 earnings season begins July 13, with S&P 500 earnings projected to grow 23.3% year-over-year. Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, JPMorgan and Bank of America report Tuesday; BlackRock and Morgan Stanley Wednesday.
- **Fed politics.** The Fed is in what Warsh called a "family fight" over tightening; markets were last pricing a quarter-point hike as soon as September.
- **Geopolitics.** Attacks continued in the Strait of Hormuz where shipping slowed; the ceasefire looks tenuous, though oil stayed relatively tame. Friday closed higher: the S&P 500 gained 0.4%, the Nasdaq 100 advanced 0.3%, and SK Hynix ADRs jumped 12.8% after the largest-ever US listing by a foreign company.

## 3. Factor Leadership: Momentum > Value
Momentum is being rewarded, concentrated in **Tech (XLK Momentum 96)** and **Energy (XLE 76)**, while defensives lag on momentum but lead Low-Vol (XLP **94**, XLU **91**, XLRE **89**). This mirrors the earnings backdrop: energy is expected to lead earnings growth, followed by technology, while healthcare anticipates a decline. Small-caps show strength too (IWM Value **87**, Momentum **84**), consistent with about 63% of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 50-day averages, up from 50% a month ago — a sign of healthy breadth.

## 4. Notable Movers
- **AMD**: Momentum **100**, RSI 69, 12-1 mom **+213.8%** — extreme trend, near overbought.
- **GOOGL**: 12-1 mom **+101.2%**, Momentum 94.
- **SNOW**: Momentum 98 but Quality **4** — a momentum-without-quality outlier.
- **Crypto capitulation**: BTC 12-1 mom **−40%**, ETH −52%, ADA −71% (RSI 46, Low-Vol 4); the whole complex sits deep below 52w highs.
- **Oversold**: DOGE (RSI 36), NFLX (RSI 38), SLV (RSI 39).
- **Value/rate proxies**: TLT Value **100**, ABBV Value **98**, XLC Value **96**.

## 5. Themes to Watch
- **CPI composition (Jul 14)** — core, not the soft headline, drives the September hike debate.
- **Bank earnings** as a tape-setter, then **ASML/TSMC** for chip-trade durability.
- **Warsh's congressional testimony (Tue)** for rate-path clues.
- **Strait of Hormuz / oil** — the swing factor for energy leadership and inflation. If oil holds after declining from its mid-May peak, the rapid energy-sector earnings growth will be over in Q3.
- **Momentum concentration risk** in mega-cap AI names if rate fears resurface.
